summary:
Accelerating climate volatility, unpredictable droughts, and degraded soil are breaking traditional farming calendars worldwide. We developed Stratum, a mobile-first decision platform that turns complex NASA satellite science into clear, field-specific crop rotation and planting schedules.

Stratum fuses NASA satellite observations of deep root-zone soil moisture with thirty-year historical climate patterns, local soil nutrient profiles, and short-term weather forecasts. Instead of rigid single-crop routines, the platform generates adaptive rotation strategies—such as drought-resistant grain sequences and nitrogen-rebuilding legumes—balancing water demand, soil restoration, and market income. Growers can stress-test their fields against simulated droughts before planting, evaluate clear operational weather windows, and export simple mobile advisories.

Stratum is important because it replaces guesswork with accessible planetary data. By helping farmers cut synthetic fertilizer costs, conserve scarce water supplies, and rebuild depleted soils, Stratum equips growers of all scales to adapt to a changing climate and protect global food security.
details:
What it does & How it works

Stratum · Field OS is a mobile-first crop rotation and soil regeneration platform that transforms NASA Earth observations into actionable, field-level planting decisions.

When a grower drops a pin or uses GPS to locate their field:

  1. Satellite Telemetry Assimilation: Stratum queries the NASA POWER API, extracting root-zone soil wetness (0–100 cm depth), topsoil seedbed moisture, and solar radiation assimilated from satellite missions including SMAP and MERRA-2.
  2. Hyper-Local Atmospheric Forecasts: It integrates with the Meteomatics Weather API (and Open-Meteo fallback) to evaluate 48-hour precipitation windows, temperature extremes, and wind risks down to a 1 km resolution.
  3. Subsurface Soil Profiling: It pulls digital soil map data from ISRIC SoilGrids, analyzing topsoil pH, plant-available nitrogen, soil organic carbon (SOC), and clay/sand composition.
  4. Agronomic Decision Engine: Stratum compares current soil and moisture conditions against the grower’s logged crop history. It calculates nutrient depletion, pathogen cycle intervals, and water balances to recommend the optimal subsequent crop (e.g., transitioning from nitrogen-depleting maize to a deep-rooted nitrogen-fixing legume or drought-hardy sorghum), accompanied by an agronomic explanation, risk alerts, and expected soil health improvements.
  5. Climate "What-If" Modeling: Farmers can toggle simulated climatic stress scenarios (e.g., 25% drier conditions) to stress-test their rotation plan against drought before purchasing seed.

Key Benefits

  • Zero Sensor or Hardware Costs: Provides ground-truth-level soil moisture and weather intelligence without requiring expensive in-ground IoT probes, soil lab tests, or GIS subscriptions.
  • Offline & Low-Bandwidth Resilience: Built with an embedded offline agronomical engine and client-side caching. Even in remote dead zones without cellular reception, farmers retain full access to their field plans and rotation advisories.
  • Accessible Field Interface: High-contrast retro-industrial UI optimized for high-glare sunlight on mobile screens in tractor cabs, complete with one-click printable advisory briefs for agricultural extension agents and simulated SMS dispatch for basic mobile devices.
  • True Regenerative Guidance: Balances commercial profitability with long-term soil carbon sequestration and topsoil erosion prevention.

Intended Impact

  • Climate Adaptation for Small & Mid-Sized Growers: Volatile weather patterns and shifting rainfall baselines make traditional generational planting calendars obsolete. Stratum arms farmers with satellite-backed foresight to diversify their crops and avoid catastrophic failed plantings.
  • Watershed & Soil Health: By optimizing natural biological nitrogen fixation through tailored legume and cover-crop rotations, Stratum reduces farm reliance on costly synthetic nitrogen fertilizers, curtailing chemical runoff into local waterways and curbing nitrous oxide emissions.
  • Global Food Security: Protecting soil organic matter directly increases the soil's natural water-holding capacity, helping farming communities buffer against severe multi-month droughts.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages: JavaScript (ES6+ / Modern ECMAScript), HTML5, CSS3.
    • NASA POWER API (SMAP radar/radiometer assimilations, MERRA-2 meteorological reanalysis, 30-year climatology baselines).
    • Meteomatics Weather API (Official Space Apps Global Collaborator — high-resolution 1 km NWP weather modeling).
    • ISRIC SoilGrids REST API (Global digital soil mapping of physical and chemical soil properties at 250 m resolution).
    • Google Public DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) (Real-time DNS MX record verification for grower account registration).
  • Development & Version Control: Git, GitHub, VS Code.

How the Project is Creative

Most satellite-based agricultural tools are built for enterprise desktop workstations, displaying raw geospatial heatmaps and complex spectral bands that overwhelming everyday growers.

Stratum’s creativity lies in abstraction and contextual decision synthesis:

  • Instead of showing raw indices, it synthesizes satellite moisture, soil chemistry, and weather forecast into one concrete recommendation: what to plant next, why to plant it, and when to avoid fieldwork.
  • It introduces an interactive Climate What-If Simulator, allowing farmers to manipulate environmental variables with a single tap and observe how rotation recommendations adjust in real time.
  • It bridges the digital divide with multi-channel accessibility: interactive web views, printable agronomist briefs, and low-tech cellular SMS dispatch simulation.

Factors Considered by the Team

  1. Connectivity in Rural Agriculture: Agricultural fields frequently suffer from poor or non-existent cellular coverage. We architected Stratum with an offline-first caching layer and local fallbacks so the app never fails or freezes in the field.
  2. Farmer Usability & Daylight Legibility: Real farmers do not read complex data tables in direct sunlight. We engineered high-contrast typography, large touch targets, color-coded status badges, and plain-language agronomic terminology.
  3. Data Authenticity vs. Friction: We removed default demo fields for authenticated users so every real farmer starts with a clean slate for their own acreage, added live DNS mail-server verification to prevent invalid accounts, while preserving a zero-barrier "Demo Mode" for judges and casual visitors.
  4. Data Privacy & Security: Field boundaries, GPS coordinates, and historical harvest yields are sensitive business data. All records are guarded by strict PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies tied directly to user authentication tokens.
